title: How to have a real "can-do" attitude!
text:
How to have a real "can-do" attitude!. Having gone through a procession of can openers, I was tired of ineffective can openers that a) did a poor job of cutting through the lid b) were constantly dirty from being splashed by the can's liquid contents, and c) slicing myself open on lids when taking out the trash. In addition, I also have arthritis in my hands and recurring tendonitis in my left wrist, so the top-down squeezing motion put uncomfortable pressure on my joints.

Exasperated, I finally went out and bought the Oxo Safety Can Opener, and have fallen head over heels in love. Here's why: first, like most Oxo kitchen tools, the handles are covered in a nonslip, easy to wash material. The knob is large, ergonomic, and coated in the same nonslip material. It offers little resistance, so it is easy to turn. Second, instead of the traditional can opener design that requires you to squeeze the handles together, the Oxo features parallel handles that lock together, so there is minimal pressure required.

The best feature is the fact that the lid is cut from the side, so you are not puncturing the can and forcing liquid to splash out, so the gears stay clean (especially beneficial when opening sticky liquids like condensed milk and dulce de leche). In fact, you don't ever see the gears as they cut, and it's initially easy to think that the can opener isn't doing anything. Another great feature is the nifty set of metal pincers that stick out from the side--these grab onto the lid and allow you to separate it from the can without having to touch it (and yes, the lid comes off as smooth as the sample lid packaged with the can opener).

The days of struggling with cheap, difficult to use can openers are over. No more splashed liquid (eau de tuna, anyone?), strained hands, or nasty cuts from too-sharp edges and spurs left behind. For those with arthritis, this is the perfect space-saving solution to buying an expensive electric can opener.
